scenarios.definition: Payment before any acceptance certificate for the PO
scenarios.sql: SELECT p.payment_ref AS id FROM payment_register p WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM acceptance_certificates a WHERE a.po_number = p.po_number AND a.issue_date <= p.payment_date)
scenarios.judgement: Payment modes are NEFT, RTGS and e-Payment only; advances are not modelled.

generate.tables: payment_register (payment_mode Advance, before acceptance), PAY PDFs, reconciliation records

scenarios.name: Multiple invoices against a contract
scenarios.definition: Two or more invoices on one PO
scenarios.sql: SELECT po_number AS id, COUNT(*) || ' invoices' AS detail FROM invoice_register GROUP BY po_number HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2
scenarios.judgement: Well covered.

scenarios.name: Same officer requested and approved
scenarios.definition: Approver equals the requisition's requesting officer on an Approved step
scenarios.sql: SELECT a.approval_id AS id, a.approver_officer_id AS detail FROM approvals a JOIN requisitions r ON r.requisition_id = a.requisition_id WHERE a.approver_officer_id = r.requesting_officer_id AND a.decision = 'Approved'
scenarios.ambiguous_note: About 15% of approved steps match, which is far above what a control environment would show; it most likely reflects how the generator picks approvers within a department, not a designed scenario. Treat the frequency as a possible artefact.
scenarios.judgement: Present at scale, but the volume suggests an artefact rather than a deliberate scenario; rare, clearly designed SoD cases are absent.

scenarios.name: Buyer also approved the award
scenarios.definition: tender buyer_officer_id equals award approved_by
scenarios.sql: SELECT a.award_id AS id FROM award_decisions a JOIN tender_master t ON t.tender_id = a.tender_id WHERE t.buyer_officer_id = a.approved_by
scenarios.judgement: None.

generate.tables: award_decisions.approved_by set to the tender buyer, AWD PDFs

scenarios.name: Approval bypass (PO without Competent Authority approval)
scenarios.definition: PO whose requisition has no approved Competent Authority step
scenarios.sql: SELECT p.po_number AS id FROM purchase_orders p JOIN requisitions r ON r.requisition_id = p.requisition_id WHERE r.estimated_value > 500000 AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM approvals a WHERE a.requisition_id = p.requisition_id AND a.stage = 'Competent Authority' AND a.decision = 'Approved')
scenarios.ambiguous_note: Low-value POs (≤ ₹5 lakh) skip the Competent Authority step, consistent with delegation by value.
scenarios.judgement: Not generated above ₹5 lakh.

generate.tables: approvals (Competent Authority step removed or not approved) for requisitions with POs

scenarios.name: Unauthorized status changes
scenarios.definition: Not detectable: events carry an actor but no authority rules
scenarios.sql: (computed in script)
scenarios.judgement: Not modelled.

generate.tables: procurement_audit_events with actors lacking authority or department, with documented exceptions

scenarios.name: Missing document versions
scenarios.definition: Tender with a corrigendum but no revised BID version (version 2)
scenarios.sql: SELECT c.tender_id AS id FROM (SELECT DISTINCT tender_id FROM tender_corrigenda) c WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM document_metadata d WHERE d.tender_id = c.tender_id AND d.doc_type = 'BID' AND d.version > 1)
scenarios.judgement: Every corrigendum has a revised document.

generate.tables: document_metadata/PDFs with a corrigendum but no revised tender version

scenarios.name: Inconsistent audit trail
scenarios.definition: Status events out of chronological order for a case
scenarios.sql: SELECT DISTINCT a.case_id AS id FROM procurement_audit_events a JOIN procurement_audit_events b ON b.case_id = a.case_id AND b.audit_id < a.audit_id AND b.event_at > a.event_at
scenarios.judgement: Audit trail is chronological.

generate.tables: procurement_audit_events with gaps, reordered or contradictory transitions

scenarios.name: Delayed approvals (more than 14 days)
scenarios.definition: Approval with recorded delay above 14 days
scenarios.sql: SELECT approval_id AS id, delay_days || ' days' AS detail FROM approvals WHERE delay_days > 14
scenarios.judgement: Well covered.

scenarios.name: Conflicting approval records
scenarios.definition: A requisition with both a Rejected step and a later Approved step
scenarios.sql: SELECT DISTINCT a.requisition_id AS id FROM approvals a JOIN approvals r ON r.requisition_id = a.requisition_id AND r.decision = 'Rejected' AND r.step_no < a.step_no WHERE a.decision = 'Approved'
scenarios.judgement: Not generated.

generate.tables: approvals with contradictory decisions across steps, APR PDFs
